questions.question: Which of the following Articles says that double jeopardy which says that "no person shall be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once." ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 20 (2).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Double jeopardy** means that a person cannot be prosecuted or punished for the same offense more than once.
 
• Double jeopardy is a fundamental principle of law in many countries, including the **United States and India**.
 
• The General Clauses Act of **1897** offers defense against double jeopardy as well.
 
• **Article 20(2) **of the Indian Constitution guarantees protection against double jeopardy.
 
• Article 20(2) also guarantees protection against** self-incrimination **and retroactive punishment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21(2): **

 
 
• **​**It deals with the right to life and** personal liberty**.
 
• Article 21(2) guarantees the right to a **fair trial **and due process of law.
 
 
 
• **Article 19(1):**
 
 
• It guarantees** freedom of speech**.
 
• It guarantees several other freedoms, including the **right to assemble** peacefully and the** right to practice any profession** or occupation.
 
 
 
• **Article 22(2):**
 
 
• It deals with the rights of **arrested persons.**
 
• Article 22(2) guarantees the **right to be informed **of the grounds of arrest and to consult a legal practitioner.

questions.question: The neutral point in the magnetic field of a horizontally positioned bar magnet is the:

options.text: point where the magnetic field changes direction
point where the magnetic field is the weakest
point where the magnetic field is the strongest
point where the magnetic field is zero

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** point where the magnetic field is zero.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The neutral point in the magnetic field of a horizontally positioned bar magnet is the point where the magnetic field is **zero**.
 
• This point is also known as the **magnetic equator** or the magnetic neutral axis.
 
• At this point, the magnetic field lines of the magnet are** parallel** to the surface of the earth.
 
• The location of the neutral point depends on the **strength** and **orientation** of the magnet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Magnetic field does not change direction at the** neutral point**, but rather it changes direction at the poles of the magnet.
 
• Magnetic field is not necessarily the** weakest **at the neutral point, as it can be weaker or stronger depending on the distance from the magnet and the strength of the magnet.
 
• Magnetic field is **strongest** at the poles of the magnet.

questions.question: Which is a nutritional disorder caused by vitamin B3 deficiency, leading to clinical manifestations from the skin gastrointestinal tract and nervous system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pellagra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pellagra is a nutritional disorder caused by **vitamin B3** (niacin) deficiency.
 
• Clinical manifestations of **pellagra** include skin rashes, diarrhea, dementia, and eventually death if left untreated.
 
• Vitamin B3 is important for energy production, metabolism, and **DNA repair**.
 
• Pellagra was once a common disease in the **United States**, particularly in the southern states, but it became rare after the fortification of grain products with niacin.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anaemia:**

 
 
• Anemia is a **blood condition** where the blood's capacity to carry oxygen is diminished because there are fewer red blood cells in the blood than usual.
 
• It can be caused by various factors such as** iron deficiency**, vitamin B12 deficiency, or chronic disease.
 
 
 
• **Beri Beri:**
 
 
• It is a disease caused by **thiamine **(vitamin B1) deficiency.
 
• It can lead to symptoms such as **fatigue**,** muscle weakness, and nerve damage.**
 
 
 
• **Scurvy:**
 
 
• It is a disease caused by **vitamin C** deficiency.
 
• It can lead to symptoms such as **bleeding gums**, **skin rash, and joint pain.**

questions.question: With which scientist did William Ramsay show in 1894 that air also contained an element unknown until then, which was named argon?

__
 
• William Ramsay showed in **1894** that air contained an element unknown until then, which was named **argon,** with the help of Lord Rayleigh.
 
• Lord Rayleigh was a British physicist who won the **Nobel Prize** in Physics in 1904 for his discovery of argon.
 
• The discovery of** argon**, a noble gas that does not react with other elements, was made possible by the scientific collaboration of William Ramsay and John William Strutt, better known as Lord Rayleigh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hermann Staudinger:**

 
 
• He was a **German chemist** who is known for his work on **macromolecules.**
 
• He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in **1953**.
 
 
 
• **Glenn Seaborg:**
 
 
• He was an **American chemist** who discovered several new elements.
 
• He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in **1951**.
 
 
 
• **Harold Urey:**
 
 
• He was an **American chemist **who discovered deuterium, a heavy isotope of hydrogen.
 
• He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in **1934**.

questions.question: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats meet at which of the following places in southern India?
questions.solution:
The correct solution is __**Nilgiri Hills.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats are **two parallel **mountain ranges running along the western and eastern coasts of India respectively.
 
• The Nilgiri Hills are located at the junction of the **Western and Eastern Ghats** in southern India, making it a significant geographical landmark.
 
• In India's **Northwestern **Tamil Nadu, Southern Karnataka, and Eastern Kerala, the Nilgiri Mountains are a portion of the Western Ghats.
 
• The** Moyar River** divides the Karnataka Plateau to the north from the Nilgiri Hills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satpura Hills:**

 
 
• It is located in **central India**.
 
• The range begins in** eastern Gujarat**, travels east along the Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra borders, and ends in Chhattisgarh.
 
 
 
• **Nallamala Hills:**
 
 
• It is located in the eastern part of the **Deccan Plateau**.
 
• It establishes the eastern boundary of the Indian states of **Telangana** and **Andhra Pradesh**, as well as the** Rayalaseema region**.
 
 
 
• **Mahendragiri Hills:**
 
 
• It is located in the **Eastern Ghats**.
 
• This mountain peak, located in the** Koraput district**, is the second highest in Odisha, after Deomali.

questions.question: Which of these is related to public goods?

options.text: The principle of excludability is applicable to its consumption.
There is a clear link between the producer and consumer which occurs through the payment process.
Its consumption is rivalrous in nature.
There is a possibility of free ridership in its consumption.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**There is a possibility of free ridership in its consumption**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Public goods are goods or services that are** non-excludable** and **non-rivalrous** in nature.
 
• They are available to everyone and their consumption by one person does **not diminish** their availability to others.
 
• The possibility of **free ridership **in the consumption of public goods is a key characteristic, as individuals can benefit from the good without contributing to its provision.
 
• If users don't pay for such goods, they can't be prevented from using or** accessing** them.
 
• **Multiple people **can use the good at the same time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The principle of excludability:**

 
 
• The ability of a good, service, or resource to be **restricted** to only those who can afford it is known as excludability.
 
• Excludability refers to the ability of a producer, supplier, or other managing body (such as the government) to stop** "free" **consumption of a good.
 
 
 
• **Clear link between the producer and consumer which occurs through the payment process:**
 
 
• It is more applicable to **private **goods.
 
• It is applicable where** payment** is necessary to access the good or service***.***
 
 
 
• **Its consumption is rivalrous in nature:**
 
 
• It suggests **rivalrous** consumption.
 
• It is also not applicable to public goods as their consumption** does not** reduce availability to others.

questions.question: What is the distance between the goal line and the penalty spot in football?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12 yards**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The distance between the** goal line** and the **penalty spot** in football is **12 yards**.
 
• The penalty spot is located** 12 yards away **from the goal line and is used for penalty kicks.
 
• The penalty kick is awarded when a team commits a **foul inside their own penalty area**, and the opposing team is given a free shot at goal from the penalty spot.
 
• The distance of 12 yards was established in the late **19th century** and has been used ever since.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **11 yards** is used for the width of the penalty area, which extends 11 yards from the goal line.
 
• An area of an association football pitch is called the **penalty area**, or 18-yard box (sometimes referred to less formally as the penalty box or just the box). 
 
• The ball is **deemed to be inside** the penalty area if any portion of it crosses any portion of the line defining the area.

questions.question: The Government of India is providing Ayushman Bharat Yojana, a health scheme. This type of government efforts falls under ______ of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 47.**__, [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 47 **states that it is the duty of the state to **improve public health **and provide medical aid to all citizens.
 
• **Ayushman Bharat Yojana **is a scheme launched by the Government of India in **2018** which aims to provide **health insurance coverage** to vulnerable families and individuals.
 
• It is a **nationwide public health insurance program** designed to give **low-income citizens** of the nation free access to health insurance coverage. Approximately 50% of the population is eligible for this program.
 
• For individuals in need of specialized care or hospitalization, it offers** free** secondary and tertiary healthcare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 45:**

 
 
• State shall endeavor to provide **free and compulsory education **for all children **until** they complete the age of **14 years**.
 
• This clause demonstrates a dedication to guaranteeing that all children in India have access to a** basic education** and to the universalization of elementary education.
 
 
 
• **Article 46:**
 
 
• ** **State shall promote **educational and economic interests **of the weaker sections of society.
 
• In particular, the** Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes** are among the weaker segments of the population whose educational and economic interests the State will give particular attention to.
 
 
 
• **Article 48:**
 
 
• State shall endeavor to organize **agriculture and animal husbandry** on modern and scientific lines.
 
• State shall take steps for **preserving and improving **the breeds, and prohibiting the slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the first radio show broadcast in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1923.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** first **radio broadcast in India was on **June 23, 1923,** by the **Radio Club of Bombay**.
 
• It was a** test transmission**, and the first regular broadcasting began on** July 23, 1927**, from the same club.
 
• The broadcasting was initially done in the evenings for** 30 minutes,** and the programs were mainly music concerts and talks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

 
• **Radio broadcasting** is the process of sending** audio across radio waves** to radio receivers owned by members of the general public, occasionally along with pertinent metadata.
 
• There are **now four forms** of radio broadcasting in use:
 
 
• **AM**: Electromagnetic radio waves are all around us but are invisible to the naked eye. 
 
• **FM:** The term FM refers to frequency modulation. 
 
• **DAB:** Digital Audio Broadcasting, or DAB, is an acronym. 
 
• **Internet radio**: When a radio station streams its content online, it's known as internet radio.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a qualitative measure of credit control used by the Reserve Bank of India?

A) CRR

B) Moral Suasion

C) SLR
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moral Suasion.**__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Moral suasion** is a qualitative measure of **credit control** used by the **Reserve Bank of India**.
 
• It is a **persuasive technique** used by the **central bank** to influence the behavior of the **commercial banks**.
 
• The RBI uses moral suasion to encourage banks to comply with the **policy guidelines** **and regulations** issued by the central bank.
 
• It is a **non-binding** measure and relies on the reputation and **credibility of the RBI** to convince the banks to follow the desired course of action.
 
• Other measures of credit control used by the RBI include quantitative measures such as **CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) and SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CRR (Cash reserve ratio)** is the **percentage **of deposits that banks are required to keep with the RBI as a reserve.

 
 
• It is a** quantitative measure** of **credit control** as it directly affects the liquidity and lending capacity of the banks.
 
 
 
• **SLR (Statutory Liquid **Ratio)** is the percentage of deposits that banks are required to invest in specified securities such as government bonds.
 
 
• It is also a **quantitative** measure of credit control as it restricts the funds available for lending by the banks.

questions.question: What is the crude birth rate of India as per Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__21.8%.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **crude birth rate i**s the number of live births **per 1,000** population in a given year.
 
• As per Census** 2011**, the crude birth rate of India is **0.218**.
 
• This means that for every** 1,000 people** in India, **0.218 births** occurred in the year **2011**.
 
• It is important to note that the crude birth rate is influenced by various factors such as **age **structure of the population, **fertility rate**, and** socio-economic factors**.
 
• In India, the crude birth rate has been declining over the years. For instance, it was **23.8 in 1991**, **22.8 in 2001**, and **21.8 in 2011**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** ratio **of all** live births** in a population during a given year to all** mid-year population** for that same year is called the crude birth rate.
 
• It is one of the key factors regulating a **nation's population growth** and is multiplied by **1000**.
 
• The formula for** CBR =** **(number of births) *1000 / estimated population at mid-year**.
 
• Population growth is calculated using the **birth rate, mortality, and migration rates**.

questions.question: NABARD launched a special pilot project in 2004 - 05 called _______ mainly to fulfil the credit needs of the small and marginal farmers and tenant farmers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**JLGs**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **JLGs** stands for Joint Liability Groups.
 
• NABARD launched the JLGs scheme in 2004-05 to cater to the credit needs of small and marginal farmers, tenant farmers, and other vulnerable groups.
 
• The primary objective of JLGs is to improve the flow of credit to tenant farmers cultivating land as oral lessees, sharecroppers, and small farmers who do not have proper title to their landholding.
 
• By forming JLGs, these farmers can avail of credit without providing any collateral security, thereby ensuring financial inclusion and improving their livelihood.
 
• JLGs operate based on mutual guarantee, where each member of the group is responsible for the repayment of loans taken by any member of the group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NABARD** (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) is an apex development financial institution in India, established on 12th July 1982.
 
• NABARD's primary focus is on the development of agriculture and rural areas through various credit and non-credit initiatives.
 
• The JLG model encourages group lending and ensures that credit is available to those who might otherwise be excluded from the formal banking system.
 
• Other initiatives by NABARD include SHG-Bank Linkage Program (SBLP), Micro-Enterprise Development Program (MEDP), and various other schemes aimed at rural development and financial inclusion.
 
• NABARD also plays a crucial role in policy planning, capacity building, and providing refinance support to rural financial institutions.

questions.question: Rajarajeshwara Temple of Tanjore was built by the ruler of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chola**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajarajeshwara Temple** is also known as **Brihadeeswarar Temple** and is located in the city of **Thanjavur** (formerly known as Tanjore) in Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• The temple was built by the **Chola dynasty** ruler **Rajaraja Chola I** in the **11th** century AD.
 
• The temple is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and is considered one of the best examples of** Dravidian architecture** in India.
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and has a **towering vimana (temple tower)** that is one of the tallest in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Pandya:**

 
 
• **​**The Pandya dynasty ruled over parts of South India, including **Tamil Nadu**, in the** 6th-17th **centuries AD. 
 
• **Maravarman Sundara I** established the groundwork for the Pandya empire in southern India around the beginning of the thirteenth century. 
 
• The pinnacles of Pandya architecture are, in fact, the** Meenakshi Temple **in Madurai and the** Aranganathar Temple in Srirangam. **
 
 
 
• **Pallava:**
 
 
• **​**The Pallava dynasty was an early medieval South Indian dynasty that ruled from the** 3rd-9th** centuries AD.
 
• They were known for their patronage of the **arts and architecture.**
 
• The **Shore Temple** and the **Vaikuntha Perumal Temple **in Kanchipuram are two of the best specimens of Pallava art and architecture.
 
 
 
• **Chola:**
 
 
• **​**The Chola dynasty was one of the most powerful South Indian dynasties that ruled from the **9th-13th** centuries AD.
 
• They were known for their **military conquests, administrative skills, and patronage of the arts**. 
 
• The** Brihadisvara Temple** in Thanjavur, the** Airavatesvara Temple **in Darasuram, and the **Brihadisvara Temple** in Gangaikonda Cholapuram are the three well-known temples that date back to the Chola era.
 
 
 
• **Chera:**
 
 
• The Chera dynasty was an ancient dynasty that ruled over parts of South India, including present-day Kerala and Tamil Nadu, from the **3rd **century BC to the **12th** century AD.
 
• **Kerala's Thiruvanchikulam Temple**, which is devoted to **Lord Shiva** and has a distinctive architectural style, is situated in the Ernakulam district.

questions.question: Under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, how many minimum days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial year has to be provided to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **100**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **100 **days of guaranteed wage employment in every financial year has to be provided to every household whose adult members volunteer to do** unskilled** manual work under the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)**.
 
• The MGNREGA was enacted in **2005** to provide a legal guarantee of **100 days** of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult.
 
• By generating **long-lasting assets**, raising **rural people standards of living**, and** lowering poverty,** the program seeks to give those living in poverty in rural areas security of income. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act** (MGNREGA) is a social security measure that aims to provide employment and livelihood security to **rural households** in India.
 
• The MGNREGA is implemented by the** Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India**, and is the largest employment generation programme in the world.
 
• The Act aims to create durable assets and infrastructure in **rural areas**, enhance the livelihoods of rural households, and promote **sustainable developmen**t in rural India.

questions.question: Manju Barggavee won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award of 2019 for which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manju Barggavee** won the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** of **2019** for the dance form **Kuchipudi**.
 
• Actress and dancer Manju Bhargavi is most known for her roles in the Telugu blockbusters **Sankarabharanam (1980) and Nayakudu Vinayakudu (1980).**
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi,** India's National Academy of Music, Dance, and Drama, gives the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. 
 
• It is the** greatest honor** bestowed upon those working in the performing arts in India.
 
• The prize included a **tamrapatra **(a brass plaque), an **angavastram** (a shawl), a citation, and Rs.** 1,00,000.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical Indian dance form that originated in the village of **Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh**, India.
 
• **Mohiniattam** is a classical Indian dance form that originated in **Kerala**, India.
 
 
• It is known for its **graceful movements and expressions.**
 
 
 
• **Chhau** is a** semi-classical **Indian dance form that originated in the eastern states of India, primarily in **West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand**.
 
 
• It involves **acrobatic movements** and martial arts.
 
 
 
• **Kathak **is a classical Indian dance form that originated in **Northern India**.
 
 
• It is known for its** fast footwork **and intricate** hand movements.**

questions.question: Sal, acacia, and bamboo, which are types of Dry Tropical Forest, receive what amount of annual rainfall?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**from**____** 51 cm to 151 cm**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dry Tropical Forests** are characterized by a** long dry season **and a** short rainy season**.
 
• **Sal, acacia, and bamboo** are some of the common tree species found in Dry Tropical Forests.
 
• These forests receive an **annual rainfall** ranging from** 51 cm to 151 cm**, which is **lower** than the rainfall received by other forest types.
 
• This are found between **10o and 25o** latitude.
 
• These forests are important habitats for a variety of wildlife species and provide various **ecosystem services**, such as carbon sequestration, soil conservation, and water regulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sal** is a tree species found in tropical and subtropical regions of **Asia and Africa**.

 
 
• It is also known as **Shorea robusta**.
 
 
 
• **Acacia** is a genus of trees and shrubs found in arid and semi-arid regions of **Africa, Australia, and the Americas**.
 
 
• ​Based on the African species **Acacia nilotica,** it was first described by the Swedish scientist Carl Linnaeus in 1773. 
 
 
 
• **Bamboo** is a type of grass that grows in tropical and subtropical regions of** Asia, Africa, and the Americas**.
 
 
• **The Indian Forest Act, 1927** considered it a **tree**. Accordingly, cutting bamboo from outside forests and transporting it was made unlawful.
 
• **In 2017 **an amendment was made to the Indian Forest Act, 1927 and bamboo has been **removed from the tree category.**

questions.question: Which of the following ministries of the Government of India has under it the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Science and Technology**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Council of Industrial Research** (CSIR) was established in **1942 **and has its headquarters in **New Delhi**.
 
• The **CSIR** has a network of** 38 national laboratories** and** 39 outreach** centers spread across the country.
 
• The **Council of Scientific undefined Industrial Research** (CSIR) comes under the **Ministry of Science and Technology**.
 
• **CSIR** is a premier national organization in India and is among the world's l**argest publicly funded organization.**
 
• The** Ministry of Science and Technology** is responsible for promoting the development and application of science and technology in various sectors of the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Ministry of Commerce and Industry** is responsible for **formulating and implementing policies** for the promotion of internal, external trade and commerce in India as well as for the promotion of industrial development in India.
 
• The **Ministry of Earth Sciences **is responsible for **promoting sustainable development** of oceans, atmosphere, and other natural resources and provide weather and climate-related services to various sectors of the economy.
 
• The** Ministry of Education** is responsible for the **formulation of policies, laying down of norms, and standards for education in India**.
